Travel information

Practical notes for a safari. Health decisions belong to your doctor. Visa decisions belong to the official government site for your passport.

Visas

Kenya asks most visitors to apply for an electronic travel authorisation before they fly. Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda each publish their own eVisa or visa-on-arrival rules. Some passports can use an East Africa tourist visa covering Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda. We send the official link that matches your nationality when we quote. Do not buy a visa from a random third-party advert.

Health

See a travel clinic four to six weeks before departure. Much of the safari circuit is a malaria area, and prophylaxis is a medical decision, not one we make for you. Yellow fever certificates are required on some routes, especially if you enter from a country where the disease is present. Carry the certificate if your clinic or the destination says you need it.

Flights

Kenya trips use Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi, code NBO. Tanzania trips use Kilimanjaro or Arusha, and we can book the hop from Nairobi. Uganda uses Entebbe, code EBB. Rwanda uses Kigali, code KGL. Tell us the flight number and we confirm who will meet you.

Packing

  • Neutral colours: khaki, olive, brown. Leave the bright blue at home.
  • A warm layer for dawn drives. The Mara and the crater rim are cold before sunrise.
  • A scarf or buff against dust, a hat, and sunscreen.
  • Binoculars. A phone camera is enough for most people. A dust cover helps if you bring a longer lens.
  • Soft bag rather than a hard suitcase. Light aircraft have a weight limit, often 15 kilograms in soft luggage.
  • Any prescription medicine in original packaging, plus a basic personal kit. Lodges are not pharmacies.

Tipping

Tips are not included and they are not a fee. Guests often give the guide about USD 10 to 20 per guest per day, and a similar pooled amount for camp staff, shared across the group. Give it at the end, in US dollars or local currency, and only if the service earned it.

Money and safety

Cards work in Nairobi and in larger lodges. Small shops and tips are easier with cash. Use ATMs in the city, not a promise of one in the park. Book through a company that will show you a licence, meet you in arrivals, and keep the same phone number from the first email to the last day.

On game drives, stay seated in the vehicle unless the guide says the park allows a walk. Do not ask the driver to leave the road for a photograph.

Common questions

What is the best time to visit Kenya?

June to October is the dry season and the usual window for the Mara River crossings. January to March is hot, drier, and quieter, with clear Kilimanjaro mornings. April and May are the long rains: some camps close, the parks are green, and prices drop. The month-by-month page covers Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda as well.

Do I need a visa?

Most visitors to Kenya apply for an electronic travel authorisation before flying, on the official government site. Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda have their own eVisa or visa-on-arrival rules, and an East Africa tourist visa can cover Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda for some passports. Rules change. We send the current official link for your nationality before you pay a deposit, and we do not guess on the form.

Are the safaris private?

Yes. The itineraries on this site are private unless a page says otherwise. You get your own vehicle and guide. Group departures are arranged when several parties want the same month. We do not publish dates we cannot run.

Which safari is best for a first visit?

For Kenya, Amboseli plus the Mara, with Nakuru if you have five or more days. For Tanzania, Tarangire, the Serengeti and Ngorongoro. Add gorillas only if you have the extra days and the permit budget. A first trip that tries to do all four countries is usually too much driving.

Can I add a beach?

Yes. Diani, Watamu and Mombasa are the Kenya coast. Zanzibar is the usual add-on after a Tanzania safari, and it also works after a Kenya trip if you fly. Plan three or four nights. One night is an airport exercise.

How much does a safari cost?

A private mid-range Kenya safari is often in the range shown on each trip, per person sharing. Two people in a private vehicle cost more per person than four. Luxury camps and gorilla permits move the figure sharply. The costs article explains what is inside the number. The quote we email is the price.

How do I pay, and what if I cancel?

A 30 percent deposit confirms the trip. The balance is due 60 days before arrival. Cancellation terms, and the stricter rules on gorilla permits, are on the booking policy page and are repeated on your invoice.

Is the Mara River crossing guaranteed?

No. Crossings usually fall between July and October and they happen when the herds decide. We plan those months if a crossing is the reason for the trip, and we say clearly that a particular morning cannot be promised.
